s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was first proposed in 1991 by which of the following persons?
x: The National Rural Employment Guarantee legislation was first proposed in 1991 by P. V. Narasimha Rao.
tq: Use the person–proposal association rather than the later enactment date.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial implementation of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: It began in 200 districts on 2 February 2006.
It began in 150 most backward districts in 2004.
It began in all districts on 1 April 2008.
It began in 625 districts on 2 October 2009.
x: The Act was launched on 2 February 2006 in 200 districts. The all-district coverage was achieved later, from 1 April 2008.
tq: Distinguish the initial coverage from later nationwide expansion.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the expansion of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act:
1. An additional 130 districts were covered during 2007–08.
2. All districts were brought under the programme from 1 April 2008.
3. The programme initially covered 625 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the programme initially covered 200 districts; 625 refers to later all-district coverage, not the initial launch.
tq: Split the statements by separating initial coverage from later expansion.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, was passed in which month and year?
x: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in September 2005.
tq: Distinguish the enactment date from the launch and renaming dates.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: With effect from 1 July 2026, which legislation replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: National Food for Work Programme Act, 2004
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
x: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, replaced MGNREGA and came into force on 1 July 2026.
tq: Identify the exact official title in a scheme-renaming and replacement question.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the guaranteed wage employment and the period over which the programme is operated are respectively:
x: VB-G RAM G provides 125 days of employment per household and operates over 305 days.
tq: Compare the paired numerical features instead of recalling either number in isolation.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025?
o: Funding pattern — Entirely demand-driven Central funding
Seasonal pause — States may pause works for up to 60 days during sowing and harvest
Wage payment — Only once at the end of the financial year
x: States may pause works for up to 60 days during sowing and harvest. VB-G RAM G has a 60:40 funding pattern, a 9 per cent administrative cost ceiling and weekly or fortnightly wage payment.
tq: Find the one correctly matched feature among swapped policy provisions.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: The funding pattern under the VB-G RAM G Act is correctly stated as:
o: Entirely financed by the Central Government
50:50 between Centre and States in all regions
60:40 between Centre and States, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Union Territories
90:10 between Centre and States in all States
x: The general funding pattern is 60:40, while the ratio is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Union Territories.
tq: Check the general ratio and its stated regional exception.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority areas of works under VB-G RAM G?
x: The four priority areas are water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood infrastructure, and extreme-weather or disaster-related works. Urban metro-rail development is not included.
tq: Eliminate the option outside the specified four-category framework.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements about the additional provisions of VB-G RAM G is correct?
o: Contractors are made compulsory for all works.
The statutory wage floor is fixed at ₹250 per day.
Job cards are renamed Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards.
Assets are recorded only in NREGASoft.
x: Under VB-G RAM G, job cards become Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards. The Act prohibits contractors, places assets on the VB-NRIS stack and specifies a statutory wage floor of ₹300 per day.
tq: Use exact terminology to distinguish renamed instruments from existing systems.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Under MGNREGA, the unit to which the employment guarantee is attached is:
o: Each adult individual in a rural area
Each registered worker in a Gram Panchayat
x: The entitlement under MGNREGA is provided to a household, not separately to every individual adult.
tq: Discriminate between the household-based entitlement and an individual-based interpretation.

s: Which provision of the Constitution is associated with the right to work that provides the Directive Principles basis for MGNREGA?
x: MGNREGA is anchored in Article 41, which relates to the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
tq: Match the policy objective with the relevant constitutional article.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the target group and objectives of MGNREGA:
1. It covers rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
2. It seeks to reduce distress migration.
3. It is primarily intended for urban skilled workers.
4. It includes natural resource management and durable asset creation among its objectives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because MGNREGA targets rural households volunteering for unskilled manual work, not urban skilled workers.
tq: Identify the target group first, then test the associated objectives.

s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry for MGNREGA?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
x: MGNREGA is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
tq: Use the ministry–scheme association and avoid neighbouring ministry substitutions.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which statement regarding wages under MGNREGA is correct?
o: The wage is fixed by Gram Sabhas and paid after one financial year.
The wage is State-specific and notified, and payment is made through Aadhaar-linked accounts by DBT.
The wage is determined by the World Bank and credited to any unregistered account.
The wage is uniform throughout India and is paid only in cash.
x: MGNREGA wages are State-specific and notified. They are transferred through DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts.
tq: Ask who fixes the wage and how the payment is transferred.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Wages under MGNREGA are required to be paid within how many days of the work done?
x: MGNREGA wages are to be paid within 15 days of the work done. Delay attracts compensation.
tq: Use the precise statutory time limit rather than the broader idea of timely payment.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: What is the minimum share of women prescribed among MGNREGA beneficiaries?
x: At least one-third of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be women, although their actual share has consistently exceeded 50 per cent of person-days.
tq: Distinguish the statutory minimum from the actual participation trend.

s: Which pair is correctly matched in the context of MGNREGA monitoring?
o: Bhuvan — GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging platform; NREGASoft — Management Information System
Bhuvan — Wage payment authority; NREGASoft — Social audit forum
GeoMGNREGA — Constitutional provision; NREGASoft — Central Finance Commission
NREGASoft — Satellite launch vehicle; Bhuvan — Unemployment allowance portal
x: Bhuvan, developed by ISRO, supports GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging, while NREGASoft is the programme's Management Information System.
tq: Start from the sure technology–function pair and reject swapped institutional roles.

s: Social audit of MGNREGA works is mandatory and is conducted by:
x: Social audit is mandatory under MGNREGA and is conducted by the Gram Sabha. Gram Sabhas also plan and monitor works.
tq: Identify the local participatory body responsible for the function.

s: If employment is not provided within 15 days of an application under MGNREGA, the unemployment allowance is at least:
o: One-fourth of the wage throughout the period
One-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
One-half of the wage for the first 30 days and one-fourth thereafter
The full wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
x: The unemployment allowance is at least one-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter.
tq: Track the change in rate after the first 30-day period.

s: Which of the following is an example of convergence under MGNREGA?
o: Replacing Gram Sabha monitoring with private contractors
Providing urban metro employment through the PMRY portal
Providing 90 or 95 person-days to PMAY-G beneficiaries through the AwaasSoft–NREGASoft link
Transferring all MGNREGA works to the Ministry of Commerce
x: MGNREGA converges with PMAY-G by providing 90 or 95 person-days to eligible beneficiaries through the AwaasSoft–NREGASoft link.
tq: Recognise convergence from the linked scheme and digital platform.

s: The annual scale of MGNREGA is broadly represented by which of the following ranges?
x: The broad annual scale is about 5–6 crore households and 200–250 crore person-days.
tq: Match the two related scale indicators rather than selecting an isolated figure.

s: Which one of the following is classified as a self-employment programme rather than a wage-employment programme?
x: PMEGP is a self-employment programme. NREP, SGRY and NFFWP are wage-employment programmes.
tq: Separate programmes by the nature of employment created, not by their rural focus.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NREP — Wage employment
2. IRDP — Self-employment
3. MGNREGS — Wage employment
4. NRLM — Wage employment
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: NREP and MGNREGS are wage-employment programmes, while IRDP is a self-employment programme. NRLM belongs to the self-employment group, so pair 4 is incorrect.
tq: Classify each programme before checking the coded combination.

s: PMRY, introduced in 1993, was primarily intended for:
x: The Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana, or PMRY, was intended for educated unemployed youth and was a self-employment programme.
tq: Link the scheme acronym with its distinctive target group.

s: The Food for Work Programme was started in 1977 during the government led by:
x: The Food for Work Programme was started in 1977 by the Janata government.
tq: Use the year–government association while distinguishing it from NFFWP.

s: The National Food for Work Programme was launched on 14 November 2004 in:
o: All 200 districts covered initially by NREGA
x: NFFWP was launched on 14 November 2004 in the 150 most backward districts.
tq: Retain both the launch date and the precise district count.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between NFFWP, SGRY and NREGA?
o: NFFWP and SGRY were created after NREGA in 2009.
NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006.
Only SGRY was subsumed into NFFWP in 2010.
NREGA was subsumed into SGRY in 2004.
x: NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in the districts covered by NREGA from 2006. The 2009 event was the addition of the name Mahatma Gandhi, not the merger of NFFWP.
tq: Use the sequence of predecessor programmes and avoid the renaming-year trap.

s:
Arrange the following employment programmes in chronological order of their introduction:
A. Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme
B. Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas
C. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
D. Employment Assurance Scheme
x: DWCRA was introduced in 1982, RLEGP in 1983, JRY in 1989 and EAS in 1993. Therefore, the correct order is B, A, C, D.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two middle programmes.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. IRDP
b. NREP
c. DWCRA
d. RLEGP

List-II (Year)
i. 1982
ii. 1978–79
iii. 1980
iv. 1983

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: IRDP dates from 1978–79, NREP from 1980, DWCRA from 1982 and RLEGP from 1983.
tq: Start from the distinctive year associations and eliminate codes with a swapped pair.

s: IRDP was extended to all development blocks on:
x: IRDP was introduced in 1978–79 and extended to all development blocks on 2 October 1980.
tq: Distinguish the programme's initial year from the later nationwide block coverage date.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SGRY was introduced in 2001. JRY dates from 1989, SGSY/JGSY from 1 April 1999, and NFFWP from 2004.
tq: Find the correctly matched year after checking the neighbouring programme dates.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the chronological position of NREGA and VB-G RAM G in the employment-programme sequence?
o: NREGA — 2006; VB-G RAM G — 2025 Act, in force from 1 July 2026
NREGA — 1999; VB-G RAM G — 2025 Act, in force from 1 April 2026
x: NREGA dates from 2006. VB-G RAM G is a 2025 Act that came into force on 1 July 2026.
tq: Separate the year of enactment from the later date on which the legislation came into force.

s: The World Development Report 2014 described MGNREGA as a:
x: The World Bank's World Development Report 2014 called MGNREGA a “stellar example of rural development.”
tq: Recall the distinctive evaluative phrase and its institutional source.
sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ministry and implementing agency associated with the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Ministry of Skill Development; implemented by NSDC
Ministry of Labour and Employment; implemented by NCS
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; implemented by KVIC
Ministry of Rural Development; implemented by DRDA
x: PMEGP is administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
tq: Use the ‘who launched or implements it?’ method to distinguish neighbouring ministries and agencies.

s:
With reference to PMEGP, consider the following statements:
1. It supports new non-farm micro-enterprises in both rural and urban areas.
2. The margin-money subsidy generally ranges from 15 per cent to 35 per cent.
3. The maximum project cost is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe PMEGP: its target is new non-farm micro-enterprises, its margin money ranges from 15% to 35%, and its project caps are ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
tq: Split the statements into target, subsidy and numerical-limit components before choosing the code.

s: PMEGP was formed by integrating which two earlier programmes?
x: PMEGP, launched in 2008, was formed by combining the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).
tq: Identify the predecessor programmes rather than the ministry or beneficiary group.

s: The earlier project-cost limits under PMEGP, before the revised limits, were:
o: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services
₹20 lakh for manufacturing and ₹10 lakh for services
₹10 lakh for manufacturing and ₹5 lakh for services
₹25 lakh for manufacturing and ₹10 lakh for services
x: The earlier PMEGP limits were ₹25 lakh for manufacturing projects and ₹10 lakh for service projects; the later limits became ₹50 lakh and ₹20 lakh respectively.
tq: Compare the older and current numerical limits carefully instead of selecting the larger revised figures automatically.

s: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is primarily associated with:
o: Collateral-free credit for urban street vendors
Formal employment incentives through EPF support
Placement-linked skill development for rural poor youth
x: DDU-GKY provides placement-linked skilling for rural poor youth and has its roots in the special projects of SGSY.
tq: Match the scheme with its distinctive target group and delivery mechanism.

s: Which ministry is associated with DDU-GKY?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: DDU-GKY is a programme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
tq: Discriminate between schemes serving rural youth, urban vendors and formal-sector employees.

s: PM-SVANidhi primarily provides:
o: Long-term housing loans to rural households
Subsidised loans to traditional artisans only
Collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors
x: PM-SVANidhi provides collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors. The scheme has covered more than 75 lakh vendors.
tq: Use the target occupation—street vendors—to separate PM-SVANidhi from other credit schemes.

s: PM Vishwakarma is implemented by which ministry and covers how many traditional artisan trades?
o: Ministry of Labour and Employment; 15 trades
x: PM Vishwakarma is associated with the Ministry of MSME and covers 18 traditional artisan trades, with training, toolkits and credit support.
tq: Combine the ministry clue with the exact count to avoid confusing artisan and skilling schemes.

s: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan, launched in 2020, was designed as a 125-day campaign for returnee migrant workers in:
x: The campaign covered 116 districts in six States and was intended for returnee migrant workers.
tq: Read the duration, district count and State count as separate numerical clues.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: National Career Service — Labour and Employment — job-matching portal
Recognition of Prior Learning — Housing and Urban Affairs — street-vendor credit
PM-SVANidhi — Rural Development — rural youth skilling
x: The National Career Service belongs to the Labour and Employment domain and functions as a job-matching portal. The other pairs interchange the functions or ministries of different schemes.
tq: Start with the sure ministry-function pair and eliminate the swapped combinations.

s: The National Career Service had more than how many employers registered?
x: The National Career Service had more than 47.21 lakh employers registered.
tq: Distinguish lakh and crore scales before comparing the numerical options.

s: Recognition of Prior Learning under PMKVY is intended to:
o: Provide working capital to street vendors
Certify existing skills against the National Skills Qualifications Framework
Provide EPF support for new formal jobs
x: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that individuals already possess against the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
tq: Identify the scheme by the action it performs—assessment and certification of existing skills.

s:
Arrange the following initiatives in chronological order of their launch or introduction:
A. PMEGP
B. DDU-GKY
C. National Career Service
D. Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan
x: PMEGP dates to 2008, DDU-GKY to 2014, National Career Service to 2015, and Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan to 2020.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest initiatives first, then place the two middle-year programmes.

s: PMEGP met its target of creating how many new micro-enterprises, with what indicated distribution?
o: 4.02 lakh; 80 per cent rural and 40 per cent women
7.50 lakh; 40 per cent rural and 80 per cent women
4.02 crore; 80 per cent urban and 40 per cent women
2.50 lakh; 50 per cent rural and 35 per cent women
x: PMEGP met its target of 4.02 lakh new micro-enterprises; 80% were rural and 40% involved women.
tq: Keep the absolute figure separate from the two percentage distributions.

s: Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY), introduced under Aatmanirbhar Bharat 3.0, primarily provided:
o: Margin money for rural non-farm enterprises
EPF-linked incentives for new formal jobs
Certification of artisan skills under NSQF
x: ABRY incentivised the creation of new formal jobs by providing support linked to the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF).
tq: Match the scheme with its distinctive instrument—EPF support for formal employment.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the PM-Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana?
o: Launched on 15 August 2025, with an outlay of ₹99,446 crore and a target of 3.5 crore jobs in two years
Launched in 2020, with an outlay of ₹50,000 crore and a target of 125 lakh migrant workers
Launched on 26 January 2026, with an outlay of ₹25,000 crore and a target of 4.02 lakh enterprises
Launched in 2015, with an outlay of ₹47,210 crore and a target of 75 lakh employers
x: PM-Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana was launched on 15 August 2025, carries an outlay of ₹99,446 crore and targets 3.5 crore jobs over two years.
tq: Check the date, outlay and employment target together; famous-scheme traps often alter one figure.

s: Andhra Pradesh ranked what position nationally under MGNREGS?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranked fourth nationally under MGNREGS.
tq: Use the exact rank rather than assuming that a major-performing State occupied the first position.

s: Under the new Mission, Andhra Pradesh pooled rural development funds to provide how many days of employment in distressed rural pockets?
x: Andhra Pradesh pooled rural development funds to provide 125 days in distressed rural pockets under the new Mission.
tq: Separate the State-level extension from the standard figures commonly associated with employment guarantees.

s: During April–July 2026, the combined MGNREGA and VB-G RAM G programmes generated approximately how many person-days?
x: The two programmes generated only about 70 crore person-days during April–July 2026, which was 43% below the previous two-year average.
tq: Anchor the period first and then distinguish the actual person-days from the percentage shortfall.

s: The 70 crore person-days generated during April–July 2026 were approximately what percentage below the previous two-year average?
x: The figure was 43% below the previous two-year average, with the decline attributed to the transition limbo.
tq: Do not confuse the absolute output figure with the percentage comparison.

s: Which combination of demands was made by unions in relation to VB-G RAM G?
o: Extension to urban areas, 125 days and ₹500 wage
Abolition of wage employment and ₹700 pension
Replacement by PMEGP, 100 days and ₹350 wage
Rollback of the scheme, 200 days of employment and ₹700 wage
x: Unions sought rollback of VB-G RAM G, 200 days of employment and a wage of ₹700.
tq: Retain the three-part demand as a single issue-specific combination.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Supreme Court Bench discussed whether the right to work should be placed on a par with Article 21.
2. Olga Tellis (1985) linked livelihood with Article 21.
3. MGNREGA is described as the only law built on the right to work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: the Supreme Court discussion concerned the relationship between the right to work and Article 21, Olga Tellis linked livelihood to Article 21, and MGNREGA is described as the only law based on the right to work.
tq: Test the constitutional case, judicial discussion and broader significance as separate statements.

s: Which of the following best expresses the wider significance of MGNREGA?
o: It certifies prior learning under the NSQF.
It is primarily an urban credit programme for informal workers.
It serves as a safety net during agrarian distress and crises such as COVID-19.
x: MGNREGA is significant as a safety net during agrarian distress and emergencies such as the COVID-19 crisis, in addition to being associated with the right to work.
tq: Apply the scheme’s broader social-protection role to a crisis situation.
